**Novelty (originality, unexpectedness): 4**
Why? The solution moves beyond standard Western-centric auditing and compliance frameworks by proposing "co-construction" of quality. The integration of culturally specific gamification (e.g., "Tolerance Jenga," "Dice of Destruction") and localized metaphors for quality management (e.g., "Souk of Errors," "Defect Mountain") is highly original and unexpected in a supply-chain context. It drops a point only because the underlying Hofstede dimensions and nearshoring strategies are well-established foundations, but their application here is remarkably fresh.

**Usefulness/Feasibility (practicality, implementability): 4**
Why? The plan is highly actionable, featuring a clear 6-week timeline, specific 90-day KPIs, defined governance structures, and concrete tool recommendations (Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp, SupplierHub). The "Double-Track Documentation" (pictograms for operators, PDFs for engineers) is a brilliant, highly practical workaround for shop-floor literacy variations. It loses a point because some elements—such as developing custom voice-annotated AI training models or organizing family-participation workshops—may be cost- and time-prohibitive within a rapid 90-day nearshoring pivot.

**Flexibility (multiple approaches, adaptability): 5**
Why? The solution is exceptionally adaptable. It provides distinct, tailored approaches for three different regions rather than a "one-size-fits-all" mandate. Furthermore, it builds flexibility directly into the process through mechanisms like the "Virtual Escalation Firebreak," the "Fail-Safe Mechanism" (rolling back to Phase 2 if KPIs aren't met), and the "Supplier Human Library," which allows the system to learn and adapt from its own mistakes. The tripartite 3C model (Clarify, Co-create, Certify) is also modular enough to be applied to future regions.

**Elaboration (detail, development): 5**
Why? The depth of this solution is outstanding. It leaves virtually no operational stone unturned, detailing everything from high-level oversight boards to shop-floor visual management. The inclusion of specific regional regulatory frameworks (NMX, NM 08.1.002, TCVN), localized training hour requirements, festival calendars (Ramadan, Tet, Día de los Muertos), and a comprehensive 10-part appendix demonstrates an exceptional level of development and thoroughness. 

**Cultural Sensitivity (cross-cultural appropriateness): 5**
Why? This is the crowning achievement of the solution. It deeply respects the distinct cultural rhythms, communication styles, and social hierarchies of Mexico, Morocco, and Vietnam. By replacing blunt, direct escalation with culturally safe alternatives (e.g., utilizing "Elders Councils" in Morocco, preserving "face" in Vietnam through indirect feedback mechanisms, and leveraging relationship-building in Mexico), the plan avoids ethnocentric imposition. It honors local traditions (tea rituals, red envelopes, local metaphors) to build genuine trust rather than just forcing compliance.
